findings.text: The opening explains what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, so a newcomer can say what it is and why it matters.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable.

findings.text: The page explains why a page about Athena is mostly about another project, which heads off the obvious confusion.
findings.source: Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim

findings.text: The second section, which should prove the opening's promise of a commit traceable to models, cost and verdict, shows only an error. The newcomer never sees Athena's own output.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown"

findings.text: The next steps are concrete: prerequisites, clone, install and a first command to try, with a jump link from the header. A newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" / "./setup.sh" / "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: This header link is not explained. A first-time visitor is not an owner and cannot tell what proposals are meant.
findings.source: Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision.

findings.text: After the header, almost all of the page is a dense study of firstmate, with exit codes, locks and capacity rules. It suits a firstmate reader, not a newcomer deciding whether to try Athena.
findings.source: Transitions (cards t1–t12) and Claims and sources (c1–c45)

findings.text: Several glossary entries say the term is not defined, so the reader is left with terms that have no working meaning. This is honest, but it doesn't help understanding.
findings.source: Glossary: "The firstmate source does not define a captain call." (similar for durable record, endpoint, heartbeat, wake)

findings.text: This points at an internal folder the visitor cannot see. It means nothing to someone reading the published page.
findings.source: About this page: "is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
